I am 73 years old, and I have farmed these 4.1 mu for 55 years. I only finished primary school, and I do not read farming books. My father taught me, and now I watch Lao Zhang and Lao Li across the lane. If their field looks good, I copy them. Last year I split my land like this: 2 mu for cotton, 1.8 mu for wheat then maize on the same plot, and 0.3 mu for stevia near the well. This year I will do the same, because change is dangerous and my grandson’s school fees must be paid.

For cotton, I will plough the 2 mu in early April with my small tractor. I buy 3 jin of improved cotton seed — the pink-coated kind from the dealer in Quzhou town, 35 yuan per jin. I sow it by hand. I spread two 50-kilogram bags of compound fertilizer on the 2 mu as base — one bag per mu. When the plants flower, I top-dress with 15 kilograms of urea per mu. At full boll I add another 10 kilograms of urea per mu. I irrigate four times from my well: planting water, flowering, peak boll, and late boll in August. I spray pesticide five times — I buy two bottles each time from the cooperative, because the bollworm never sleeps. I expect 280 kilograms of seed cotton per mu.

For wheat, I rotary-till the 1.8 mu in early October. I sow Jimai improved seed, 25 jin per mu. I put half a bag of DAP and almost one full 50-kilogram bag of urea on the 1.8 mu as base fertilizer. I do not buy potassium for wheat — I tried it ten years ago and saw no difference, so I save that 180 yuan. I irrigate three times: wintering water in November, jointing water in March, and grain-filling water in April if the sky stays dry. I spray fungicide twice. I expect 420 kilograms per mu.

For maize, I plant the 1.8 mu right after wheat harvest in mid-June. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, 4 jin total. I do not till; I plant directly into the wheat stubble. At planting I put 20 kilograms of compound fertilizer per mu, and when the plants are knee-high I add 30 kilograms of urea per mu. I irrigate twice: once after planting if the June heat is strong, and once at tasseling. I spray twice for armyworm. I expect 500 kilograms per mu.

For stevia, the 0.3 mu plot is small. I dig it with a hand hoe. I put 200 kilograms of pig manure on it. I buy one 5-kilogram bag of urea and spread half now, half later. I water three times together with the cotton. I spray once for aphids. I expect 150 kilograms of fresh leaves per mu.

Why this plan? Because last year I did exactly this, and I paid the bills. My son works off-farm and sends some money, but fertilizer prices went up, so I cannot experiment. I saw Lao Li try a new cotton variety two years ago and the bolls rotted, so I stick to my coated seed. I would rather spend an extra 30 yuan on urea than lose yield — a bad harvest means my grandson’s school fees disappear. If cotton prices rise this autumn, maybe next spring I buy one more bag of compound fertilizer. But this year, I stay safe.
